title: Resolve Multi-Model Disagreements Through Bounded Executable Discriminating Challenges
target_platform: Hybrid multi-model debate harness; evaluating-agent-work; deterministic Python/shell execution sandbox (ceiling 900k tokens, 6 CPU-hours)
hypothesis: For disputed engineering claims, requiring each side to propose a bounded executable challenge will: (a) resolve >= 80% of disputes correctly; (b) outperform the better of majority voting and prose debate by >= 15 percentage points; (c) keep confidently incorrect resolutions <= 5%; and (d) use <= 3 challenge rounds per dispute within an equal inference budget.
falsification_criteria: Any threshold missed falsifies the hypothesis. A dispute settled by an LLM judge without running an available discriminating test is not an executable resolution. A test passing in one isolated environment does not prove a universal claim.
experiment: Use 60 hidden-oracle disputes about small programs, concurrency traces, accounting transformations, and dependency behavior. Create correct-vs-incorrect and both-incorrect pairs. Randomize vendor assignments. Compare majority voting, bounded prose debate, and executable challenges in disposable testbeds.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Frontier models are permitted as adversarial debaters; total inference ceiling is 900k tokens.

related_missions.MISSION-013: EXTENDS: converts prose debates into empirical test-generating adversarial trials.
related_missions.MISSION-036: CONSUMES: grounds dispute outcomes in formal evidence contracts.
related_missions.MISSION-041: REUSES: leverages automated property-based counterexample machinery to generate challenge cases.
